Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet) BACnet points list

Updated 7 November 2026

Short answer

The Acuvim 3 exposes 2,164 read-only Analog Inputs and 76 Binary Inputs, the same on BACnet IP and BACnet MS/TP: real-time values, sequence components, THD and individual harmonics (magnitude and angle), flicker, demand by quadrant and direction, accumulated energy, and I/O module counters, analog values and DI / relay status.

This page lists 2240 BACnet objects for the Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet) — 0 of them writable — with each object’s type, instance number, name, engineering units and access. It is re-typed from Accuenergy’s own free documentation, linked below.

BMS integration notes: Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet)

Integration in brief

All objects are read-only measurements. Map system power, energy, demand, PF, current and voltage; most of the 2,240 objects are harmonics and only needed for power quality work.

Minimum points to map

The short list most integrators start with — enough to run the unit from a BMS. Map more as the job needs.

ObjectNameWhyAccess
AI 18System Active PowerSystem real power, kWRead
AI 2056Accumulative System Active Energy-ImportImported energy total, kWhRead
AI 1972System Active Power Demand-ImportImport kW demandRead
AI 34System Power FactorSystem power factorRead
AI 14Average CurrentAverage current, ARead
AI 2Phase A Line-to-Neutral VoltagePhase A L-N voltage, VRead
AI 1System FrequencyFrequency, HzRead

Network setup

  • BACnet IP and BACnet MS/TP expose the same object set.

Watch out for

  • About 1,780 objects are individual harmonic values; don't poll them all on a slow MS/TP trunk.
  • Set a COV increment before subscribing; the default of 0 reports every change (IP only).

Integration notes

  • I/O module objects (DI counters, DI status, AI, AO, relay status) only carry data when that module (IO01, IO11-IO14, IO21-IO24, IO31-IO34) is fitted.
  • COV increment is supported on BACnet IP only; the default COV increment is 0 on every AI.
  • The spreadsheet's notes sheet names the firmware 'Acuvim-S v1.04p13'; the title says Acuvim-3.
  • Source: Accuenergy 'BACnet Points List Acuvim-3' spreadsheet, firmware v1.04p13, generated 2026-10-06.

Questions about the Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet)

How many BACnet points does the Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet) have?

This list has 2240 BACnet objects: 2164 analog inputs, 76 binary inputs. The exact set on a given unit depends on its firmware, installed options and configuration.

Which Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet) BACnet points are writable?

None of the listed objects are marked writable in the source documentation.

Where is the official Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet) BACnet documentation?

The source is BACnet Points List Acuvim-3, revision 2026-10-06, published free by Accuenergy at https://www.accuenergy.com/wp-content/uploads/Acuvim-3_BACnet-Object-List.xlsx.

What are the minimum BACnet points to integrate the Accuenergy Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet)?

Start with AI 18 System Active Power (System real power, kW); AI 2056 Accumulative System Active Energy-Import (Imported energy total, kWh); AI 1972 System Active Power Demand-Import (Import kW demand); AI 34 System Power Factor (System power factor); AI 14 Average Current (Average current, A); AI 2 Phase A Line-to-Neutral Voltage (Phase A L-N voltage, V); AI 1 System Frequency (Frequency, Hz).

How do I check these points on the real Acuvim 3 power quality meter (BACnet)?

Scan the network with a BACnet IP browser such as Easy BACnet, open the device and compare its object list with this table. Anything missing is usually an option that isn't installed or a point that is disabled in the controller's configuration.
